accuracy_findings.claim: The lex [[lex/upgrade_xp]] is not a tradition, despite its name.

accuracy_findings.claim: {table:traditions} row 'Myrmezir, The Ariance Charter, +10 % Dominion Tax Rate'
accuracy_findings.problem: The bonus is an additive +0.1 on dominion_rate (base 0.3 goes to 0.4, so 30% becomes 40%). The table prints it as '+10 %', the same form it uses for multiplicative bonuses such as '+25 % Frigate Ships' Initial XP'. A reader can take it as x1.1 (30% to 33%).
accuracy_findings.evidence: The probe shows dominion_rate=0.3 for the other factions and 0.4 for Myrmezir at slow, medium and fast. faction.ex: myrmezir_late %Core.Bonus{from: :direct, to: :dominion_rate, type: :add, value: 0.1}.
accuracy_findings.fix: In the generator's effect formatting (effect_md / bonus formatting for add bonuses on rate targets), print percentage points for additive rate bonuses (for example '+10 points Dominion Tax Rate'), or handle it wherever dominion_rate is formatted for all bonus tables.

clarity_findings.claim: Two sentences describe where traditions appear on screen: "The faction panel lists your faction's traditions. The faction picker shows each faction's traditions before you join."
clarity_findings.problem: Style rule 8 allows UI location to be described in at most one sentence of words. The brief's OWNS item 2 ("where you see them") is one thing, but the page spends a whole paragraph and two sentences on it. Nothing is lint-flagged, but this breaks the rule 8 limit.
clarity_findings.fix: Merge into one sentence, for example "You can see them on the faction panel and in the faction picker before you join." Optionally list a shot_request for the faction panel with a box on the traditions list, since the brief allows a shot.

clarity_findings.claim: "They are the same in Legacy, Tactic and Flash games, measured in ticks. See [[game-time]]."
clarity_findings.problem: "measured in ticks" does not fit: traditions are not measured in anything, so the clause dangles and the game-time pointer looks unmotivated. The reader has to guess what is measured in ticks. Only the amounts in the table are per tick, and the table prints its own legend.
clarity_findings.fix: End the sentence at "...Legacy, Tactic and Flash games." (or "at every game speed"). Drop the ticks clause. Keep "See [[game-time]]." only if you want to point at speeds, with a lead such as "Speeds are explained in [[game-time]]."

clarity_findings.claim: The first sentence is "Every faction has four traditions: three bonuses and one drawback."
clarity_findings.problem: Rule 5 asks the first sentence to say what the thing is. This gives the count but never defines a tradition, so a new reader does not learn it is a permanent faction-wide effect until the next sentence. The table also does not mark which row is the drawback, so the reader has to infer it from the sign of the effect.
clarity_findings.fix: Open with a definition, for example "A tradition is a permanent bonus or drawback that comes with your faction." Then give the count ("Each faction has four: three bonuses and one drawback.") and keep the always-on and can't-change sentences.

votes.reason: The page is a clean, scannable table and the "three bonuses and one drawback" framing is clear. A few effect names are unexplained, and nothing on it relates to rising prices.
stumbles: Drawbacks aren't labelled. "Mercenary: +5 % Armed Forces Maintenance" is a drawback but carries a plus sign, and "-10 % Armed Forces Maintenance" is a bonus. I had to work out which of the four rows per faction was the bad one myself.

"They are the same in Legacy, Tactic and Flash games, measured in ticks." reads as if the traditions are measured in ticks. It's unclear whether it means the game modes or the numbers, and the sentence is easy to misread.

Several effects aren't explained or linked: "Siderian Propaganda", "Erased Removal", "Erased Infiltration", "Frigate Ships' Initial XP", "Armed Forces Bombing", "+20 Intelligence". As a first-week player I don't know what they do.

Nothing on the page says whether traditions affect what patents or lexes cost. I came here wondering why prices keep rising and got no answer, only the passing line that "Navarch Tradition" is a lex and not a tradition.

votes.reason: The page is a clean four-per-faction table with a short intro, so a skimming player gets the rule fast; only a few unit and wording ambiguities remain.
stumbles: "+25 % Frigate Ships' Initial XP" / "-10 % Armed Forces Maintenance": the page doesn't say what the percent applies to (base value, upkeep total, only new ships?), and "Armed Forces" is not defined or linked.

"+20 Intelligence" has no unit or link, and "+20 % Siderian Propaganda", "+15 % Erased Removal" and "+15 % Erased Infiltration" are plain text with no link to what they do, unlike Technology and Ideology.

"Production, credit, technology, ideology and upkeep amounts are per tick.": the note only covers some rows, and the intro's "measured in ticks" reads oddly next to the rows that show +3 / +60/h. It is unclear whether "-5 % Credit" or "+10 % Defense" are percent modifiers or flat amounts.

votes.reason: A skimming player gets the rule fast (four fixed perks per faction, always on, unchangeable) and the table is easy to scan, but the effect wording has a few unexplained terms and a mixed-unit note.

The percentage effects ("+25 % Frigate Ships' Initial XP", "+20 % Siderian Propaganda") have no stated base, so it's unclear whether a percentage is per hour or one-off.

"Legacy and Tactic games also have a lex named Navarch Tradition. It is a lex, not a tradition." This aside is helpful but unexpected, and "resource tooltips ... appear under Traditions" doesn't tell me where to find non-resource effects like Intelligence or Defense. votes.reason: The page clearly says what a tradition is and how to spot each faction's drawback. It says nothing about rising patent or lex prices, so a player asking that finds no answer, and a few effect names go unexplained.
stumbles: The page never mentions prices, patents or why costs rise. The only pointer is "Legacy and Tactic games also have a lex named Navarch Tradition. It is a lex, not a tradition." That doesn't help a player wondering why prices go up.
The footnote says "upkeep amounts are per tick", but the table calls the same thing "Armed Forces Maintenance". It is unclear that upkeep and maintenance are one thing.

Several effect names are not explained or linked: "Siderian Propaganda", "Erased Removal", "Erased Infiltration", "Armed Forces Bombing", "Armed Forces Repair" and "+20 Intelligence". A first-week player can't tell what they do.

votes.reason: The table gives each faction's four traditions and the intro says which row is the drawback, but a skimmer has to work out a few bonus-versus-drawback cases and a few effect names by themselves.
stumbles: "In the table below, each faction's drawback is its last row. The sign alone doesn't tell you which is which." Paying more upkeep is a drawback, but the table doesn't mark the row, so I had to lean on the row order. It is clear once read, but a skimmer might miss it.

"-10 % Armed Forces Maintenance" versus "+5 % Armed Forces Maintenance": the text says maintenance is the fleet upkeep, but the table says "Maintenance" and the intro says "upkeep". The footnote also lists "upkeep amounts are per tick" although no upkeep figure appears in the table.

Some effect names are opaque with no link or explanation: "+25 % Frigate Ships' Initial XP", "+20 Intelligence" (a flat number, not a percentage), "+15 % Armed Forces Bombing", "+15 % Erased Removal" and "+15 % Erased Infiltration". The page doesn't say what they change or where else they appear.
